content: A rash accompanied by fever can present in patients across all age groups. Fever is typically defined as a body temperature of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher, or as a sensation of warmth to the touch, or a subjective history of feeling feverish. This clinical finding is common in both children and adults. In adults, the occurrence of a rash with fever can be attributed to a variety of underlying causes, including allergic reactions, immune-mediated disorders, and infections. Infectious agents often induce rashes through mechanisms such as toxin production or immunogenic reactions to antigens. These infectious agents may be viral or bacterial in origin. Examples of such pathogens include the Rubeola virus, Staphylococcus aureus, and Borrelia burgdorferi. Among allergic reactions, adverse drug reactions are the most frequently associated with the presentation of a rash and fever. The clinical manifestations in affected patients can vary widely, ranging from mild flu-like symptoms, as seen in Lyme disease, to severe and potentially life-threatening conditions, such as toxic shock syndrome caused by Staphylococcus aureus. Life-threatening causes of rash with fever include conditions that, if left untreated, may result in death or irreversible disability within 24 hours.
